headline: Profit rises as catastrophe losses widen combined ratio
summary_short: AXIS Capital's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 7.3% y/y to $1.753 billion and diluted EPS grew 24.3% y/y to $3.38, even as elevated catastrophe and Middle East conflict losses pushed the combined ratio to 93.1% from 88.9% a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue grew 7.3% y/y to $1.753 billion, driven by 15% growth in Insurance net premiums earned (professional, marine, and liability lines), partly offset by a 3% decline in Reinsurance premiums (liability, professional, and motor lines). The combined ratio rose 4.2 points y/y to 93.1%, as $80 million of catastrophe and Middle East conflict losses (5.3 points) outweighed $15 million of favorable prior-year reserve releases; underwriting income was $143 million. Net income rose 15.6% y/y to $258.1 million; diluted EPS reached $3.38 (+24.3% y/y). AXIS repurchased $97 million of stock and paid $0.44 per share in dividends; book value per diluted share rose to $80.67. The filing states no new forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by increases in professional lines, marine and aviation, and liability lines in Insurance, partially offset by declines in Reinsurance liability, professional, and motor lines.
Growth reflects premium growth and $22 million of strategic capital partner fees, partly offset by a 4.2-point rise in the combined ratio from elevated catastrophe and conflict losses.
Rise tracks higher net premiums earned and underwriting income, partially offset by the wider combined ratio from catastrophe and conflict losses this quarter.
EPS growth outpaced net income growth because diluted shares outstanding fell to about 74.2 million from 79.3 million a year earlier, reflecting share buybacks.
Management's highlights emphasized underwriting income of $143 million, a 93.1% combined ratio, and continued capital return via a $97 million buyback and $0.44 per-share dividend.
